content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in Portland

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: PMI requires either a bachelor's degree plus three years of project-management experience, or a high school diploma plus five years. Document your work history and educational credentials now—you'll need them for your PMI application. Verify you meet the baseline before enrolling.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Training
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual PMP Bootcamp, delivered by active certified practitioners. Attend interactive instructor-led sessions on your schedule—no commute required. You'll cover the full PMBOK® Guide framework and exam domains across our structured curriculum.

steps_items.heading: Apply to PMI and Pay Exam Fee
steps_items.text: After finishing your training hours, submit your PMI application and required documentation. Pay the examination fee directly to PMI. PMI will verify your eligibility; approval typically follows within days. Keep your confirmation details for exam registration.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Sit for the Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources—practice questions, study guides, and instructor office hours—to reinforce your learning. Schedule your exam once PMI approves your application. The proctored exam is delivered online; you'll receive your pass/fail result immediately.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your PMP® Credential
steps_items.text: PMP® certification is valid for three years. Earn Professional Development Units (PDUs) through approved training, volunteer work, or published contributions to stay current. Renew before expiration by submitting your PDU record and renewal fee to PMI.
